title: Decorating a callable object with an async call runs it once and never retries
text_original: Third and last PR after breaking down https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/433 (follows https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/437). After DRYing the `iter()` function and making `AsyncRetrying` support `async` callbacks, add new `async` strategies (basically a copy-paste) and improve typing.
text_rewritten: Our clients are objects rather than functions: the class implements `__call__` as a coroutine and we decorate the instance. The decorator routes it to the synchronous retry path, so the target is invoked exactly once, the coroutine object it returns is recorded as a successful result, and the caller gets an un-started coroutine back. Awaiting that coroutine afterwards runs the body a single time with no retrying whatsoever, which means a transient failure just propagates. Rewriting the same logic as a module-level coroutine function retries correctly, so the difference is entirely in how the decorator decides whether the target is asynchronous — it appears to recognise only plain coroutine functions and not other callables whose call is a coroutine. Plain synchronous and plain asynchronous targets must keep the dispatch they have today.

acceptance_hint: Decorating an instance whose `__call__` is a coroutine yields an awaitable that retries the body until it succeeds; plain synchronous functions still return their value directly and plain coroutine functions still behave exactly as before.
